issue_context.title: Add additional exit codes for `gh cache delete --all`
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

I use `gh cache delete --all` to purge all cache related to a workflow that stores ephemeral items in cache.

* When cache items are present and they are successfully removed, the command returns an exit code of 0.
* When no cache items are present, the command returns an exit code of 1.

Unless I parse standard error to read the message for the first case, I can't disambiguate it between an invocation that did not find any cache to remove, and one that did but failed to successfully remove it.

### Proposed solution

I propose a unique exit code for the specific case where no cache items were found. This would allow callers to treat this use case as a success and disambiguate it from any genuine errors.

This would simplify its usage for this use case significantly.

### Additional context

According to the [manual](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_help_exit-codes), it appears this would not fall outside of the cli's existing behavior.
comments:
For some background, typically, if you are specifying a resource directly, we treat it as a failure since silently failing to remove the resource you expected to can be quite frustrating. That's why `gh cache delete <cache-id>` will error if the cache-id isn't found.

However, in this case, what the user is trying to convey is "I want all caches gone" and we can indicate they are all gone with a `0` exit code. The same error behaviour exists over on [`codespace delete --all`](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/9b9e654c767d58b666063715169cb24c92551f06/pkg/cmd/codespace/delete.go#L172) but there's also no test for it so I'm not sure how much that behaviour was cared about.

The question is, is there anyone out there who might be relying on the current behaviour. This is technically a breaking change, I'm just trying to figure out whether it would matter. It seems _unlikely_.

Also, I wonder if it's possible to disambiguate "there are no caches" and "this token doesn't have permission to see the caches". Both might return `404`? If these were indistinguishable, returning `0` for `--all` could be tricky.

I'm going to put a `discuss` label on this for the team to chat.

> Also, I wonder if it's possible to disambiguate "there are no caches" and "this token doesn't have permission to see the caches". Both might return 404? If these were indistinguishable, returning 0 for --all could be tricky.

It looks like listing caches and deleting caches both only require `repo` scope, and that's required for `gh` to work so this doesn't appear to be an issue https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/cache?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-github-actions-caches-for-a-repository

In the interest of not breaking backwards compatibility, I'm going to suggest the introduction of a new flag here `--succeed-on-no-caches`. This should only be usable with `--all`. I'm not looking to introduce idempotent deletes on singular resources, since that will be a large new UX across the entire CLI.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** I have no caches
**When** I run `gh cache delete --all --succeed-on-no-caches`
**Then** it exits `0`

**When** I run `gh cache delete <cache-id> --succeed-on-no-caches`
**Then** I get an error that `--succeed-on-no-caches` can only be used in conjunction with `--all`

review_comments: I don't see this enhancement in the issue request. Can you tell me why you added them?

Added this to improve the UX. Fetching caches takes some time.
Currently, the progress indicator only covers the DELETE verb i.e. the actual deletion of caches, not fetching part.

Here's an example:

```shell
$ time gh cache delete --all --repo iamazeem/test
X No caches to delete

real	0m0.767s
user	0m0.089s
sys	0m0.019s
```

From a user perspective, the progress indicator in this case made sense especially for high latency networks.
LMK if you think it's not needed. I'll remove it.
Nah, seems good, so we should keep this! Thanks for the explanation and for addressing this paper cut
